# Abstract

**Background and Significance**: Pancreatic cancer-related biliary obstruction is managed with biliary stent placement via ERCP. Current guidelines recommend metal biliary stents (MS) over plastic biliary stents (PS) for inoperable malignant obstruction; however, real-world comparative evidence on safety and effectiveness remains limited.

**Study Aims**: To compare the clinical safety and effectiveness of metal versus plastic biliary stents in patients with pancreatic cancer using real-world observational data from the OMOP Common Data Model.

**Study Description**:

* **Population**: Adult patients (age ≥ 18) with a prior diagnosis of pancreatic cancer who received their first biliary stent insertion, excluding those with a history of cholangiocarcinoma.

* **Comparators**: Target — Metal Biliary Stent (ATLAS Cohort ID: 688); Comparator — Plastic Biliary Stent (ATLAS Cohort ID: 689).

* **Outcomes**: Acute cholangitis (Tokyo Guideline 2018, Cohort ID: 697); Moderate acute cholangitis (Cohort ID: 719); Cholangitis broad definition (Cohort ID: 663); All-cause mortality (Cohort ID: 665); Biliary re-intervention.

* **Design**: New-user active comparator cohort study using 1:1 propensity score matching with large-scale covariates (LASSO logistic regression) and empirical calibration via negative control outcomes.

* **Timeframe**: Follow-up windows of 30, 90, 180, and 365 days from the index date (first stent insertion).

# Rationale and Background
Pancreatic cancer is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. At the time of diagnosis, the majority of patients present with biliary obstruction, which causes jaundice, pruritus, and cholangitis, significantly impairing quality of life and overall clinical status. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)-guided biliary stent placement is the standard of care for palliating malignant biliary obstruction.

Biliary stents are broadly classified by material into **Metal Biliary Stents (MS)** and **Plastic Biliary Stents (PS)**.

| Characteristic | Metal Stent | Plastic Stent |
|----------------|-------------|---------------|
| Patency Duration | Long (6–12+ months) | Short (3–6 months) |
| Cost | High | Low |
| Exchangeability | Difficult (self-expanding) | Easy |
| Need for Re-intervention | Low | High |

Current domestic and international guidelines (ESGE, ASGE, KSGE) recommend **metal stent use** in patients with inoperable malignant biliary obstruction, based on evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) showing superior patency and lower re-intervention rates compared to plastic stents [@Dumonceau2018; @Almadi2013]. However, whether these guideline recommendations are equally supported by real-world data remains uncertain.

Existing RCTs may not be representative of real-world clinical populations due to strict eligibility criteria. Real-world comparative evidence on safety (cholangitis) and effectiveness (re-intervention, survival) between the two stent types is limited. A large-scale observational study using the OHDSI Common Data Model (CDM) can validate the applicability of current guidelines in real-world settings.

# Study Objectives
The overall goal of this protocols is conducting comparative safety and effectiveness research to establish evidences for benefits and harms of metal and plastic stents in patients with pancreatic cancer through OHDSI network.

The primary objective is to compare the clinical safety and effectiveness of **metal biliary stents** versus **plastic biliary stents** in patients with pancreatic cancer-related biliary obstruction using real-world data.

Secondary objectives are:

1. To compare the incidence of **acute cholangitis** between the two stent groups
2. To compare the frequency of **biliary re-intervention** between the two stent groups
3. To compare **all-cause mortality** between the two stent groups

# Research Methods

## Study Design

This study uses `CohortMethod` [@Schuemie2020-fa].

This is a **observational study** based on a **new-user active comparator design** using the OHDSI CohortMethod package for population-level effect estimation (PLE). The new-user design mitigates immortal time bias by requiring all patients to be naive to the study exposure at cohort entry [@Suissa2008].

- **Index Date (Day 0):** Date of first biliary stent insertion (metal or plastic)
- **Baseline Period:** 365 days prior to the index date (Day −365 to Day 0)
- **Follow-up Period:** Day 1 through end of observation, death, or end of study period

## Data Sources
The analyses will be performed across a network of observational healthcare databases.  All databases have been transformed into the OMOP Common Data Model, version 5.4.  The complete specification for OMOP Common Data Model, version 5.4 is available at:  https://github.com/OHDSI/CommonDataModel

## Study Population

### Target Cohort — Metal Biliary Stent

**Definition:** Patients with pancreatic cancer who received their first metal biliary stent insertion.

**Inclusion Criteria:**

| Criterion | Window | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Metal biliary stent insertion | Day 0 | First-ever metal biliary stent insertion (Device Exposure) |
| Age ≥ 18 years | Day 0 | |
| Pancreatic cancer diagnosis | Any time before Day 0 | Any recorded diagnosis prior to or on index date |

**Exclusion Criteria:**

| Criterion | Window | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Cholangiocarcinoma diagnosis | Any time before Day 0 | Any prior diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma |

### Comparator Cohort — Plastic Biliary Stent (ATLAS Cohort ID: 689)

**Definition:** Patients with pancreatic cancer who received their first plastic biliary stent insertion.

Inclusion and exclusion criteria are identical to the target cohort, differing only in the type of stent inserted.

### Covariate Assessment Windows

| Covariate Type | Window |
|----------------|--------|
| Demographics | Day 0 |
| Short-term baseline conditions and medications | Day −30 to Day 0 |
| Long-term baseline conditions and medications | Day −365 to Day 0 |

## Exposure Comparators

### Target — Metal Biliary Stent

Metal biliary stents are identified in the OMOP CDM `DEVICE_EXPOSURE` table using concept codes representing self-expandable metal stents (SEMS) and related devices (Codeset ID: 2, including descendant concepts for fully covered SEMS).

Only the first-ever metal biliary stent insertion qualifies as the index event, fulfilling the new-user design requirement.

### Comparator — Plastic Biliary Stent

Plastic biliary stents are identified in the OMOP CDM `DEVICE_EXPOSURE` table using concept codes representing plastic biliary stent devices.

Only the first-ever plastic biliary stent insertion qualifies as the index event.

## Outcomes {#outcomes}

### Primary Outcomes

| Outcome | Cohort ID | Definition |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Acute Cholangitis (Tokyo Guideline 2018) | 697 | Clinical definition based on Tokyo Guidelines 2018 criteria (see below) |
| Moderate Acute Cholangitis | 719 | Moderate severity per Tokyo Guidelines 2018 criteria |
| Cholangitis (broad definition) | 663 | Based on diagnosis codes for cholangitis |
| All-cause Mortality | 665 | Based on CDM Death table |

### Acute Cholangitis Definition (Tokyo Guideline 2018)

The TG18/TG13 framework [@Kiriyama2018] defines acute cholangitis using three categories:

- **Suspected diagnosis**: ≥1 item from **A** + ≥1 item from **B** or **C**
- **Definite diagnosis**: ≥1 item from each of **A**, **B**, and **C**

**Operationalization in this study:** Category C (imaging) criteria cannot be reliably ascertained from structured OMOP CDM data. Therefore, acute cholangitis in this study is operationalized as **Suspected diagnosis** using Categories A and B only (≥1 item from **A** + ≥1 item from **B**).

**Category A — Systemic Inflammation**

| Criterion | Threshold | OMOP Concept ID |
|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| Fever / shaking chills | Body temperature > 38.0°C | 3020891 |
| WBC (leukocytosis) | > 10,000/mm³ | 3000905 |
| WBC (leukopenia) | < 4,000/mm³ | — |
| CRP | ≥ 1 mg/dL | — |

**Category B — Cholestasis**

| Criterion | Threshold | OMOP Concept ID |
|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| Jaundice | Total bilirubin ≥ 2.0 mg/dL | 3010156 |
| Liver enzymes | ALP, γGTP, AST, or ALT > 1.5× upper limit of normal | — |

**Category C — Imaging** *(not ascertainable from CDM; excluded from operationalization)*

| Criterion | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Biliary dilatation | Dilation of intra- or extrahepatic bile ducts on imaging |
| Evidence of etiology | Stricture, stone, stent, or other obstructing cause on imaging |

#### Severity Grading (TG18)

**Grade I (Mild):** Does not meet Grade II or III criteria; responds to initial medical treatment.

**Grade II (Moderate):** ≥2 of the following 5 criteria:

| Criterion | Threshold |
|-----------|-----------|
| WBC | > 12,000 or < 4,000/mm³ |
| Fever | ≥ 39°C |
| Age | ≥ 75 years |
| Total bilirubin | ≥ 5 mg/dL |
| Albumin | < 0.7 × lower limit of normal |

**Grade III (Severe):** ≥1 of the following organ/system dysfunctions:

| System | Criterion |
|--------|-----------|
| Cardiovascular | Hypotension requiring dopamine ≥ 5 μg/kg/min or any dose of norepinephrine |
| Neurological | Disturbance of consciousness |
| Respiratory | PaO₂/FiO₂ < 300 |
| Renal | Oliguria or serum creatinine > 2.0 mg/dL |
| Hepatic | PT-INR > 1.5 |
| Hematological | Platelet count < 100,000/mm³ |

### Biliary Re-intervention

Defined as a procedure code indicating biliary stent replacement, repair, or re-insertion occurring after Day 7 from the index date.

## Analysis

### Covariates

Propensity scores are estimated using large-scale covariate sets from the `FeatureExtraction` package. Concept codes directly related to stent insertion are excluded from the covariate set (`excludedCovariateConceptIds`).

**Included Covariates:**

| Domain | Detail | Window |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Demographics | Age group, sex, race, calendar month | Day 0 |
| Conditions | Condition Group Era | Short-term (−30 to 0) |
| Medications | Drug Group Era | Short-term (−30 to 0), Long-term (−365 to 0) |
| Measurements | Measurement values | Long-term (−365 to 0) |
| Measurement ranges | Measurement Range Group | Short-term, Long-term |
| Observations | Observation | Short-term (−30 to 0) |
| Composite indices | Charlson Comorbidity Index, DCSI, CHADS2Vasc | Day 0 |


### Propensity Score Matching

- **Model:** LASSO Logistic Regression (via `Cyclops` package)
- **Matching:** 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching without replacement
- **Caliper:** 0.2 (standardized logit scale)
- **Common Support:** Preference score-based trimming (PS trimming)

### Balance Assessment

Covariate balance before and after matching is assessed using standardized mean differences (SMD). Target threshold: all covariates SMD ≤ 0.1 (or ≤ 0.25).

### Follow-up Windows

| Analysis ID | Description | Follow-up Period |
|-------------|-------------|------------------|
| 1 | ITT 1:1 PS Matching | 90 days |
| 2 | ITT 1:1 PS Matching | 30 days |
| 3 | ITT 1:1 PS Matching | 180 days |
| 4 | ITT 1:1 PS Matching | 365 days |

All analyses apply the intent-to-treat (ITT) principle.

### Outcome Model

- **Model:** Cox Proportional Hazard Model
- **Effect Estimate:** Hazard Ratio (HR) with 95% Confidence Interval
- **Primary Reporting Timepoint:** 365 days from index date (Analysis ID 4)
- **Survival Visualization:** Kaplan-Meier survival curves

### Empirical Calibration

Negative control outcomes are used to assess and correct for residual confounding and systematic bias using the `EmpiricalCalibration` package [@Schuemie2018-pnas].

- **Negative Controls:** Outcomes with no known biological association with either stent type (see [Negative Control Concepts](#negative-control-concepts))
- **Calibration Procedure:**
  - Pre-calibration: Assess proportion of negative controls with HR = 1 within 95% CI
  - Post-calibration: Estimate and correct for systematic bias; derive calibrated effect estimates

# Sample Size and Study Power {#sample-size}

This is a retrospective cohort study using existing electronic health records. Sample sizes are determined by available data rather than pre-specified power calculations.

Available sample sizes prior to matching:

| Group | N |
|-------|---|
| Metal biliary stent (Target) | 1,273 |
| Plastic biliary stent (Comparator) | 870 |

Power calculations will be conducted based on observed event rates for each outcome. Adequate power is anticipated for the primary outcomes (acute cholangitis and re-intervention) given expected event rates. Statistical power for all-cause mortality analyses may be limited due to the overall poor prognosis of pancreatic cancer.

# Strengths and Limitations {#strengths-limitations}

## Strengths

1. **Real-world data:** Reflects actual clinical populations including patients excluded from RCTs due to strict eligibility criteria
2. **Large-scale propensity score matching:** Hundreds of covariates used for robust confounding control
3. **Empirical calibration:** Quantitative assessment and correction of residual confounding and systematic bias using negative control outcomes
4. **OHDSI standard methodology:** Reproducible and transparent analytical framework
5. **Multiple follow-up windows:** Evaluation at 30, 90, 180, and 365 days covers diverse clinically relevant timepoints

## Limitations

1. **Observational study limitations:** Absence of randomization means unmeasured confounding cannot be fully excluded
2. **Single database:** Generalizability of results may be limited
3. **Outcome misclassification — acute cholangitis:** The TG18 definite diagnosis requires imaging evidence of biliary obstruction or dilatation (Category C); however, structured imaging findings are not reliably captured in the OMOP CDM. Consequently, acute cholangitis is operationalized using a **suspected diagnosis** criterion (Categories A + B only), which may result in outcome misclassification. Cases meeting only laboratory criteria without imaging confirmation may represent other etiologies, potentially inflating the observed incidence of cholangitis.

# Protection of Human Subjects

The study is using only de-identified data. Confidentiality of patient records will be maintained at all times. All study reports will contain aggregate data only and will not identify individual patients or physicians.

# Management and Reporting of Adverse Events and Adverse Reactions

This is a non-interventional, retrospective observational study using existing electronic health records. No investigational products are administered and no direct patient interventions are performed. Accordingly, formal adverse event monitoring and reporting procedures applicable to interventional studies are not required. Any incidental findings of clinical significance identified during data analysis will be handled in accordance with applicable institutional policies.

# Plans for Disseminating and Communicating Study Results
The study results will be posted on the OHDSI website after completion of the study. At least one paper describing the study and its results will be written and submitted for publication to a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

## Biliary Re-intervention

**Definition:** A biliary re-intervention event is defined as any procedure code indicating biliary stent replacement, reinsertion, or repair occurring after Day 7 from the index date (first stent insertion).

**Identification:** Biliary re-intervention is identified using the same concept sets as the exposure cohorts (metal or plastic biliary stent device exposure codes). An event is counted as a re-intervention if it occurs more than 7 days after the index date, regardless of the stent type used at re-intervention.

**Rationale for Day 7 washout:** Events within the first 7 days post-index are excluded to avoid misclassifying planned staged procedures or early technical corrections as re-interventions.
